summary: Defines the MIME types associated with MP4 files and recommends which registered type to use depending on the kind of content. This helps servers and mail programs label audio and video files correctly. It is standards-track and was later updated by RFC 6381.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 4337 decides which label to put on an MP4 file. An MP4 file is a container that may hold video, audio, interactive scene information, or none of those, so the label has to say what is really inside. The document registers three types for ordinary MP4 files, one for video, one for audio and one for everything else, plus two types for the Initial Object Descriptor, which describes a presentation.

questions: which media type should mp4 audio use
subtitle: Which MIME type to put on an MP4 file, depending on whether it holds video, audio or neither.

tldr.problem: An MP4 file is a container, so it can hold video, audio, scene information or none of those, and a server had no agreed way to label the file for the kind of content inside it.
tldr.mechanism: The document registers five media types, video/mp4, audio/mp4, application/mp4, application/mpeg4-iod and application/mpeg4-iod-xmt, and gives a rule for choosing between them based on the contents.
tldr.outcome: Servers and mail programs can now label an MP4 file with a type that says what is inside it. RFC 4337 was later updated by RFC 6381.

today: RFC 4337 was published in March 2006 as a Proposed Standard and has since been updated by RFC 6381. The registrations it made are the standard labels for MP4 files.

sections.title: MPEG-4 and the MP4 File Format
sections.content:
The document describes a standard definition of MIME types associated with MP4 files and the guidelines for using them.

MPEG-4, also known as ISO/IEC 14496, is a standard designed for the representation and delivery of multimedia information over a variety of transport protocols. It includes interactive scene management and visual and audio representations, as well as system functionality like multiplexing, synchronization, and an object descriptor framework.

The historical approach for MPEG data has been to declare it under "video", and this approach is followed for ISO/IEC 14496. In addition, some MIME types are defined under "audio" and "application" for the streams not containing visual presentation.

Amendment 1 of the ISO/IEC 14496 standard, also known as version 2, introduced a standard file type, called MP4 files, for encapsulating ISO/IEC 14496 data. This is now separately specified as the MP4 file format, which in turn is based on the ISO base media file format. A separate specification covers the storage of Advanced Video Coding material, also known as H.264, in files based on the ISO base media file format. The MP4 file type can be used in a number of ways, perhaps the most important of which is its use as an interchange format for ISO/IEC 14496 data, as a content-download format, and as the format read by streaming media servers.

These first two uses will be greatly facilitated if there is a standard MIME type for serving these files, for example over HTTP. The ISO/IEC 14496 standard is broad, and therefore the type of data that may be in such a file can vary. Simple compressed video and audio, using a number of different compression algorithms, can be included, as can interactive scene information, metadata about the presentation, and references to ISO/IEC 14496 media streams outside the file. Different top-level MIME types are used to identify the type of the contents in the file.
sections.plainLanguage: MP4 is a container format, so the file extension alone does not tell a server what is inside. The label on the file has to say whether it is video, sound, or something else.

sections.title: Selecting the MIME Type
sections.content:
The MIME types to be assigned to MP4 files are selected according to the contents. The document gives three basic guidelines.

First, if the file contains neither visual nor audio presentations, but only, for example, MPEG-J or MPEG-7, use application/mp4. Second, for all other files, including those that have MPEG-J and similar content in addition to video or audio streams, video/mp4 should be used. Third, for files with audio but no visual aspect, including those that have MPEG-J and similar content in addition to audio streams, audio/mp4 may be used.

In any case, these indicate files conforming to the MP4 specification, ISO/IEC 14496-1:2000, systems file format.
sections.plainLanguage: Video present means the video label. No video but audio present means the audio label is allowed. Neither means the application label. Any extra content such as scene information does not change the choice.

sections.title: The Five Media Type Registrations
sections.content:
This section describes the MIME types and names to be used with various MPEG-4 contents, and registers five new MIME types with IANA.

The first three, video/mp4, audio/mp4 and application/mp4, are all MP4 files as defined by ISO/IEC 14496-1:2001, with different names for the three kinds of content. The other two, application/mpeg4-iod and application/mpeg4-iod-xmt, cover the Initial Object Descriptor, which describes a presentation, in binary form and in textual form respectively.

All five registrations share the same additional information. None of them has a magic number. The file extensions mp4 and mpg4 are both declared, and the Macintosh File Type Code mpg4 is registered with Apple. The person to contact for information and the author and change controller is David Singer, the ISO/IEC 14496 file format chair. The intended usage of all five is Common. None of the registrations has a required parameter or an optional parameter.

For the three MP4 file types, the published specification is ISO/IEC 14496-1:2001. For the textual Initial Object Descriptor it is ISO/IEC 14496-1:2001 AMD2.
sections.plainLanguage: All five types were registered for common use, with no magic number and no parameters. Two file extensions, mp4 and mpg4, are declared for all of them.

sections.title: The Video and Audio MP4 Media Types
sections.content:
The first registration is the MP4 file. Its MIME media type name is video and its MIME subtype name is mp4, giving video/mp4. It has no required parameters and no optional parameters. The published specification is ISO/IEC 14496-1:2001 and the application is Multimedia.

The second registration is the MP4 file with audio but without visual presentation. Its MIME media type name is audio and its MIME subtype name is mp4, giving audio/mp4. It too has no required parameters and no optional parameters, and its published specification is ISO/IEC 14496-1:2001.

For both of these, the encoding considerations say that base64 is generally preferred, and that the files are binary and should be transmitted without CR/LF conversion or 7-bit stripping. The interoperability considerations note that a number of interoperating implementations exist within the ISO/IEC 14496 community, and that this community has reference software for reading and writing the file format.
sections.plainLanguage: One registration is the ordinary MP4 file with pictures, the other is the MP4 file with sound only. Neither takes any parameters.

sections.title: The Object Descriptor Media Types
sections.content:
The third registration is the MP4 file with an MPEG-4 System Stream and neither visual nor audio presentation. Its MIME media type name is application and its MIME subtype name is mp4, giving application/mp4. It has no required parameters and no optional parameters, and its published specification is ISO/IEC 14496-1:2001.

The fourth registration is the Initial Object Descriptor in binary format. Its MIME media type name is application and its MIME subtype name is mpeg4-iod. Its encoding considerations say that base64 is generally preferred, and that files are binary and should be transmitted without CR/LF conversion or 7-bit stripping. Its published specification is ISO/IEC 14496-1:2001.

The fifth registration is the Initial Object Descriptor in textual format. Its MIME media type name is application and its MIME subtype name is mpeg4-iod-xmt. Its encoding considerations are none, since the format is already text, and its published specification is ISO/IEC 14496-1:2001 AMD2.
sections.plainLanguage: The application label covers a file with no pictures and no sound, such as a file holding only scene information. The two IOD types cover the descriptor that lists what a presentation contains, in binary and in text form.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
It is possible to inject non-compliant MPEG streams, audio, video and systems, in the MP4 file to overload the receiver's or decoder's buffers. This might compromise the functionality of the receiver or even crash it. This is especially true for end-to-end systems like MPEG, where the buffer models are precisely defined.

An MP4 file supports the storage of stream types, including commands that are executed on the terminal such as OD command and BIFS commands, and programmatic content such as MPEG-J, which is Java byte code, and ECMASCRIPT. It is possible to use one or more of the above in a manner non-compliant to MPEG to crash the receiver or temporarily make it unavailable.

Authentication mechanisms can be used to validate the sender and the data to prevent security problems due to non-compliant malignant MP4 files.

A security model is defined in ISO/IEC 14496 Systems for MP4 files containing MPEG-J contents, which comprises Java classes and objects. MPEG-J defines a set of Java APIs and a secure execution model. MPEG-J content can call this set of APIs and Java methods from a set of Java packages supported in the receiver within the defined security model. According to this security model, downloaded byte code is forbidden to load libraries, to define native methods, to start programs, to read or write files, or to read system properties.
sections.plainLanguage: A file can carry commands and scripts that run on the machine that plays it. The document says authentication is the way to make sure the file came from someone you trust, and it lists what downloaded code is not allowed to do.
